subject: Re: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler - POC & next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler - post-call recap & proposed POC

Tom — thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Recap
- Primary goal: reduce inference latency tails during peak events while lowering per-token unit cost vs your current hyperscaler setup.
- Key constraints: predictable capacity during marketing spikes, SOC2/compliance audit evidence, procurement timeline in August.

Redwood differentiators we touched on
- Dedicated GPU pools with capacity guarantees and burst capacity for short peaks
- Smart routing to fall back to on-demand endpoints (we can configure a fallback to public endpoints during unexpected overloads)
- Observability: token-level cost/latency breakdown, per-route dashboards for SLA verification

Proposed POC (3-week technical run)
1) Objective tests: 95th/99th percentile latency, cold-start behavior, throughput at X qps under your traffic profile.
2) Configs to compare: (A) Acme baseline on hyperscaler; (B) Redwood Dedicated reserved pool (pinned model + KV caching); (C) Redwood Dedicated with fallback to on-demand during simulated spikes.
3) Success criteria: 95th latency improvement >= 30% vs baseline OR cost per 1M tokens <= 0.8x baseline with equal latency.
4) Data we need from you: representative traffic profile (qps by hour, typical sequence lengths), peak spike window definitions, list of endpoints to test.

Next steps / timeline
- Tom: share the traffic profile and procurement contacts (Priya?) — by EOD Wed (7/22).
- Redwood: produce a POC test plan + draft SOW and send within 48 hours after we receive traffic profile.
- Technical kickoff: propose week of 7/27 if procurement is on track.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-vs-hyperscaler-brief.pdf (high-level comparison + proposed test matrix)

Let me know if I missed anything. Happy to jump on another 30–45m call to align the test matrix.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-dedicated-vs-hyperscaler-brief.pdf - application/pdf)

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.com>

Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler - post-call recap & proposed POC

Thanks Markus — appreciate the clear plan. A couple quick clarifications and I’ve attached the traffic profile.

What we sent (attachment): ACME_traffic_profile.xlsx — includes 6 months of qps by hour and payload size distribution.

Questions:
1) Pricing: can you provide a rough comparison for reserved capacity (12-month commit) vs pay-as-you-go on Redwood? We need ballpark numbers to justify to finance.
2) Capacity guarantees: during Black Friday-like spikes we saw 5–7x normal qps for ~3 hours. Will your dedicated offering guarantee capacity for that or would we rely on fallback?

We looped in Priya (procurement) — Priya, can you confirm your timeline for contract review & any specific SLA requirements?

— Tom
Tom Ellis
Sr. Director, Product Infrastructure — Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler - post-call recap & proposed POC

Tom / Markus — thanks, received the profile. Quick replies and next items from the commercial side.

1) Ballpark pricing (high level) — reserved vs pay-as-you-go
- Reserved (12m commit): ~35% discount vs on-demand for the same GPU tier + included baseline burst credits for short peaks (first 30 minutes per day).
- On-demand / pay-as-you-go: higher per-token cost but no commit; we offer automated fallback pricing when you exceed reserved capacity (billing at on-demand rates for overflow).

I’ll send a formal grid, but I included the working file here: pricing_grid_v3.csv

2) Capacity guarantees and guarantees language
- We can offer a capacity reservation for predictable sustained load. For short extreme spikes (5–7x for <4 hours) we suggest a hybrid strategy: provision reserved capacity for expected peak baseline and configure automatic burst + on-demand fallback for rare extreme events.
- We can include an SLA clause with minimum throughput guarantees and credits tied to missed availability targets — we’ll draft suggested language in the SOW.

3) Compliance / evidence
- Attached: SOC2_certificate_redwood.pdf — happy to open an NDA if you need more detailed artifacts.

Next internal steps
- Redwood will draft a POC test plan + SOW once we confirm traffic windows and target SLOs.
- Commercial: I’ll put together a formal pricing grid and a preliminary SOW for review (ETA 48 hours).

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
(attachments: pricing_grid_v3.csv - text/csv; SOC2_certificate_redwood.pdf - application/pdf)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler - post-call recap & proposed POC

Looping in a couple technical and ops notes from my side: 

- Reserved capacity discounts are tied to commit length and baseline utilization assumptions. If Acme can commit to a baseline qps for 12 months we can add an additional 5–10% volume discount.
- For Black-Friday-sized spikes (multi-hour, multi-x over baseline) we recommend:
  * Canary rollout where 10% of traffic routes to Redwood Dedicated initially; monitor latency and error rates for 48 hours.
  * If stable, ramp to 50% then 100% while autoscaling policies provision more instances.
  * Configure fallback routing to Acme’s hyperscaler endpoints for overflow — we’ll capture overflow metrics so you can reconcile billing vs usage.
- We can explicitly add burst capacity credits (e.g., 4 hours/month at no additional cost) into the SOW for trial customers to cover demo/marketing events.

I’ll draft the technical test matrix for the POC (latency percentiles, cold-start, KV cache hit rates) and share on the DocSend link.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
